questions.prompt: What is the difference between a stored property and a computed property in Swift? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that stored properties allocate memory to store constants or variables
Explains that computed properties calculate values on demand using getters and setters
Mentions that computed properties do not allocate storage for values

questions.modelAnswer: In Swift, stored properties allocate memory inside an instance to save constant or variable values directly. Computed properties do not allocate storage in the instance. Instead, computed properties provide a getter and an optional setter to calculate values on demand each time they are accessed.

questions.prompt: Why must a lazy property always be declared with var instead of let in Swift? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that lazy properties are not initialized during instance creation
States that the initial value is assigned upon first access after initialization finishes
Notes that let constants require a known value before initialization completes

questions.modelAnswer: A lazy property must always be declared with var because its initial value is not calculated during instance initialization. The value is only evaluated and assigned when the property is accessed for the first time. Because let constants must be initialized before instance initialization finishes, Swift disallows lazy let declarations.

questions.prompt: Explain how willSet and didSet property observers work. Do they fire during instance initialization? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that willSet runs immediately before a stored property changes and provides newValue
Explains that didSet runs immediately after a stored property changes and provides oldValue
States that property observers do not execute when properties are set inside an initializer

questions.modelAnswer: Property observers watch and respond to changes in a stored property. The willSet observer executes right before the value is stored and receives newValue. The didSet observer executes immediately after the value changes and receives oldValue. Property observers do not execute when a property receives its value during an initializer.

questions.prompt: Why must a read-only computed property be declared with var instead of let? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that computed properties evaluate their getter dynamically on each access
States that let constants represent fixed, immutable storage assigned once
Mentions that the returned value of a computed property can vary over time

questions.modelAnswer: A read-only computed property must be declared with var because it evaluates its getter expression dynamically on every read. Its return value can change over time if the underlying properties it depends on change. The let keyword is reserved for fixed constants stored in memory, so computed properties require var.

questions.prompt: How does declaring an instance as a let constant affect its variable stored properties for a struct versus a class? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that for a struct (value type), a let instance freezes all its properties including var properties
Explains that for a class (reference type), a let constant only locks the reference pointer
States that variable stored properties of a constant class instance can still be mutated

questions.modelAnswer: Because structures are value types, declaring a structure instance with let makes the entire instance immutable, preventing modifications to any of its var properties. In contrast, classes are reference types. Declaring a class instance with let locks the reference pointer itself, allowing variable stored properties on that instance to be mutated freely.
